newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock markets up at start of interim season.
newsitem.headline: China stock markets up at start of interim season.

text.p: China's stock markets closed higher on Monday as investors bought on optimism at the kick-off of the interim results reporting season.
Shanghai's foreign currency B shares rose two percent as foreign institutions began cautious buying at the start of the reporting season for interim results, brokers said.
The B share index ended the day up 1.522 points or 2.01 percent to 77.373 points on volume of 9.045 million shares worth $5.545 million.
Sentiment was helped after plush material maker Shanghai Haixin Co on Monday became the first B share company to post its results for the first half of 1997.
Haixin announced a 75 percent rise in net profit to 45.876 million yuan based on domestic accounting standards.
"Everyone took Haixin's results as a reason to enter the market," said an analyst at an Asian securities firm. "Foreign institutions bought selectively with an eye towards interim results."
Haixin was suspended from trading on Monday morning, but ended the day up $0.034 or 5.76 percent to $0.624 as one of the day's top gainers.
Shenzhen's B shares ended with solid gains on Monday as the recent sharp rally extended on an optimistic outlook for 1997 interim company results, analysts said.
The Hong Kong dollar-denominated B share index gained 1.88 points or 1.42 percent to 134.25 on turnover of HK$72.7 million compared with HK$87.8 million last Friday.
"We are expecting some positive interim reports," an analyst at J&A Securities (HK) said.
Analysts said investors would focus on firms seen offering good interim dividends.
Listed companies are required to report interim results by the end of August, but companies that perform poorly typically wait until shortly before the deadline to announce.
Refrigerator maker Hefei Meiling Co Ltd was the biggest winner in the Shenzhen B share market, soaring HK$0.37 or 8.01 percent to HK$4.99.
Recently-listed Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd was one of the most heavily traded Shenzhen B shares on volume of 3.1 million shares, gaining HK$0.25 to HK$7.70.
Shanghai's domestic currency A share index added to gains from Friday but investors remained wary, awaiting signs the market was headed decisively higher, brokers said.
The A index closed up 32.403 points or 2.68 percent to 1,239.260 points on volume of 533.578 million shares worth 6.476 billion yuan.
Shenzhen's A share index rose 12.80 points or 3.21 percent to 411.02 on turnover of 7.8 billion yuan against 5.6 billion yuan in the previous session.

The formal announcement on Friday that Zhou Zhengqing had taken over as head of the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) failed to drag the Shanghai and Shenzhen markets down on Monday, analysts said.
The CSRC leadership change was seen as one of the last in a series of government moves to curb stock speculation, they said.
